name: smoke-basics
description: Minimal end-to-end coverage that both engines must satisfy. Kept small and hand-written so a harness regression is obvious without reading a large fixture.
setup: UPSERT { CONCEPT ?t { {type: "$ConceptType", name: "Drug"} SET ATTRIBUTES { description: "Pharmaceutical drug" } } }
UPSERT { CONCEPT ?t { {type: "$ConceptType", name: "Symptom"} SET ATTRIBUTES { description: "Medical symptom" } } }
UPSERT { CONCEPT ?p { {type: "$PropositionType", name: "treats"} SET ATTRIBUTES { description: "Treatment relationship" } } }

cases.name: projects scalar columns
projects a whole concept node
matches a proposition and projects the link
joins a concept pattern with a proposition pattern
filters on a numeric attribute
filters with REGEX
excludes with NOT
pads unmatched rows with OPTIONAL
cases.command: FIND(?s.name, ?d.name) WHERE { ?s {type: "Symptom"} OPTIONAL { (?d, "treats", ?s) } } ORDER BY ?s.name ASC

cases.name: OPTIONAL projecting only the outer variable
OPTIONAL projecting only the inner variable

skip.rust: single-variable FIND projects the variable's distinct entity domain in Rust, so the OPTIONAL padding row is dropped and the result is ["Aspirin"]. TS projects one value per solution row and keeps the null. The spec does not settle which is right; tracked as an open question for KIP.

cases.name: counts
orders descending
upsert merges attributes and bumps _version
cases.command: UPSERT { CONCEPT ?d { {type: "Drug", name: "Aspirin"} SET ATTRIBUTES { risk_level: 1, dosage: "325mg" } } }

cases.name: the merged attributes are visible and _version advanced
EXPECT VERSION rejects a stale guard
cases.command: UPSERT { CONCEPT ?d { {type: "Drug", name: "Aspirin"} EXPECT VERSION 1 SET ATTRIBUTES { risk_level: 9 } } }

cases.name: the rejected guard left no trace
a malformed cursor is rejected rather than restarting pagination

skip.rust: the Rust engine uses base64 CBOR entity cursors, so this token fails differently; cursor encodings are a documented divergence

cases.name: a syntax error carries the grammar's own code
deleting a concept cascades to its propositions
the cascade removed the link too
